title: Associated-prime transport from the fibre module to the fibre ring
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be prime, and put $C=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, with $j:B\to C$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Let $L$ be any $C$-module, regarded as a $B$-module by restriction of scalars along $j$. Contraction along $j$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Ass}_C(L)\to\operatorname{Ass}_B(L)$. More precisely, for every $z\in L$ the ideal $J=\operatorname{Ann}_C(z)$ contracts to $I=\operatorname{Ann}_B(z)$ and satisfies $J=IC$, and $J$ is prime if and only if $I$ is prime. All primes in $\operatorname{Ass}_B(L)$ contract to $\mathfrak p$ in $A$, so this is the restriction of the fibre prime correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection]. Residue fields and tensors are [def-weil-residue-field] and [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; associated primes here mean exact annihilators of elements [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. No flatness or Noetherian assumption is imposed.
